Fivetran has been diligent the three years I was tucked away in FAANG analytics... there was a sort of holy trinity of companies that has completely dominated the analytics SaaS market: Fivetran, Snowflake, and dbt.
Ingest with Fivetran, transform with DBT and store in Snowflake. Simple, serverless, consumption based pricing etc. definitely better than the old ETL world!
Fivetran's syncing has been very reliable (compared to others we tried) but the 'active row' based pricing is unpredictable and can have huge spikes in billing costs.
we've found some of their (5T) competitors (who bill by connector) make far more sense for certain services. Love fivetran, though.

Dumb valuation aside, Airbyte seems like it will wipe the floor with Fivetran and other pay-per-record data pipelining tools. Open source, decent community, you can host it yourself... Orders of magnitude cheaper.

I have a weird vibe with Fivetran, Snowflake and Looker together as a combo with their credit based billing... Fivetran is really cool though, but you need to be careful about getting into bed with all 3 those products at once.
Unrelated to the article itself but Fivetran has the worst possible product from a developer perspective, their APIs are unreliable and will fail on you randomly.
Fivetran is so massively overpriced for the service they provide.

Be careful with fivetran - they inflate your data and then bill you for it. In our case, they inflated by ~10x the record count by doing a join between two tables/endpoints which wasn't required... We dumped them once our first credit purchase ran empty.
Fivetran created a great mid-market product that was best in class and had wide adoption. What they didn't have was a very customizable product designed for large enterprises.
not a big fan of fivetran's pricing
They charge based on the highest number of unique rows transferred for the month. It gets expensive quickly.

Fivetran's free plan has met my needs to sync data from different ad platforms to BigQuery pretty well... One of their pitfalls is charging by the row... you need to watch what data you're syncing and pare it down during the 2-week period they give you when setting up a new connector.

we did experience regular (probably once every couple of months) issues with our ETL getting out of sync. We even had to do a full re-sync on a couple of occasions (which to their credit they did for no charge).

otherwise fivetran is fantastic for not having to deal with a boatload of third parties constant API updates and changes. If your core competency is something else entirely and not doing ETL, then it's worth paying for.
Paying $1,000 for Fivetran, $2,000 for Snowflake, $2,000 for Looker seemed crazy.
dbt Cloud is an uncompelling product. Fivetran is convenient but absurdly expensive. Now dbt core development is just another marketing cost for Fivetran.
Fivetran and dbt who are detested for being overpriced and underfeatured in the segment they are supposed to be good at (ETL/ELT).

Fivetran has 2 pieces: data movement and integration/access... no one has as complete a catalog of integration plugs as Fivetran... Fivetran has become the default in getting data out of tools you already pay for directly into a controlled space.
Fivetran connects a skinny pipe (APIs) to a fat pipe (databases) while Census connects a fat pipe to a skinny pipe.
